standard.title: Significant Events, Ideas, People and Movements in an Asian Society
standard.description: significant events, ideas, people, groups and/or movements in the development of an Asian society
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have examined the features of the selected Asian society (AC9HH9K19) and the causes and effects of European contact (AC9HH9K20). They understand the structural conditions. This descriptor asks them to examine the significant individuals, groups, and movements that shaped the society's development in response to these conditions — including both those who accommodated and those who resisted colonial influence.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate significant events, ideas, people, groups and movements in the development of the selected Asian society.

nodes.label: Significant individuals and groups — reform, resistance, and modernisation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate the role of significant individuals and groups in the development of the selected Asian society, including those who promoted reform, modernisation, or resistance to European influence.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the role of one significant individual or group in the development of the selected Asian society.
nodes.typical_width: For China: describe the activities of Christian missionaries, the Self-Strengthening Movement, the Society of Righteous Harmony (Boxer Rebellion), and the role of Empress Dowager Cixi in modernising China. For Japan: examine the role of Emperor Mutsuhito (Meiji Restoration), Commodore Matthew Perry's role in opening Japan, and the Satsuma Rebellion. For India: describe the role of the British East India Company, the Sepoy Rebellion, the Indian National Congress, and key figures (Gokhale, Naoroji, Tilak, Gandhi). For Indonesia: examine contributions of Diponegoro, the Java War, Budi Utomo, Sarekat Islam, Sukarno, Hatta, and Sjahrir.
wider: Examine Mohandas K. Gandhi's early political development — from South Africa to India — and analyse how the experience of colonial injustice shaped his philosophy of non-violent resistance as a specific strategic and ethical response to British power

Investigate the Boxer Rebellion from multiple perspectives — Qing government, foreign powers, Chinese reformers, ordinary Chinese people — to examine how the same event was driven by different motivations and interpreted through different lenses

Compare nationalist leaders in two Asian societies (e.g. Gandhi in India and Sukarno in Indonesia) — examining similarities and differences in their backgrounds, methods, and the colonial contexts they confronted
nodes.hinge_reason: Specific knowledge of key individuals and events is the foundation for the perspective and interpretation analysis in K22 and K23. Students cannot compare perspectives on the significance of figures and movements without first knowing who they were and what they did.

response_modes.reason: Accurate knowledge of the key figures and movements in the selected society needs to be secured before students can use this knowledge to examine perspectives and interpretations. A structured timeline or actor-map may help students organise many names and events.

success_criteria: Investigates the role of at least two significant individuals or groups in the development of the selected Asian society
Describes what each figure or group contributed and how their contribution connected to the broader development of the society

nodes.label: Significance and interpretation of key events and movements
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the significance of key events and movements in the development of the selected Asian society, explaining why they mattered for the society's trajectory.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain why one event or movement was significant for the development of the selected Asian society.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the significance of selected events and movements for the development of the society — examining what changed as a result, who was affected, and how the event or movement connected to the society's later trajectory; explain how the same event or movement could be viewed differently by different groups at the time.
wider: Examine how a key event in the selected Asian society (e.g. the Meiji Restoration, the Boxer Rebellion, the Sepoy Rebellion) both responded to external pressure and produced internal social change — assessing the relationship between colonial pressure and domestic transformation

Investigate how nationalist movements in the selected society used both traditional cultural identity and Western-derived ideas (democracy, self-determination) to build their case — examining the ideological complexity of anti-colonial nationalism

response_modes.reason: Evaluating significance integrates the factual knowledge of events (Node 1) with the broader analytical framework of causes, effects, and perspectives — the endpoint skill for this descriptor.

success_criteria: Evaluates the significance of at least one key event or movement for the development of the selected society
Explains at least one way the same event could be viewed differently by different groups at the time
